A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DADA research. Their text, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original numerical experiments on synthetic softmax, polyhedron-feasibility and high-order worst-case objectives, including convergence and distance-estimation plots.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E retain those experiments and add an empirical sensitivity study of the initial distance estimate.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2.1 corrects its gradient/update indexing: v1 computes g_k before defining x_k, while v2 starts at k=0 and uses g_k to construct x_{k+1}. This repairs the stated procedure to match the existing analysis; the distance-adaptation rule and coefficients in (2.4) remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three synthetic optimization problem families. The added initialization sweep uses the existing softmax task and does not introduce a new dataset, domain or task requirement.

E2.justification: The corresponding performance experiments retain WDA, UGM, DoG and Prodigy, while distance-estimation plots retain DoG, Prodigy and DADA. New Table 1.1 compares theoretical properties of algorithms; it does not add experimentally evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The original protocols remain unchanged. V2 adds a sweep of the initialization factor delta from 10^-6 to 10^-1. Its exact softmax settings are inconsistently documented: Appendix E lists mu={0.5,0.1,0.01}, whereas Figure E.5 labels {0.1,0.01,0.005}.

E4.justification: New Figure E.5 tests sensitivity to the initial distance estimate over six settings. Existing smoothness sweeps and distance-estimation analyses are retained, mostly relocated to Appendix E.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added sensitivity study likewise presents curves without statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: All five original plots are retained unchanged. Figure E.5 adds nearly overlapping convergence curves across six initializations. V2 also newly states that Prodigy eventually reaches similar accuracy to the best methods, although the unchanged p=2 panel does not demonstrate that.

T1.justification: V2 introduces proper closed extended-valued objectives, subdifferentiability on Q and an interior-domain minimizer assumption. Appendix D replaces Appendix C's assumptions over Q with local-ball conditions for five function classes, adding a radius restriction and 1/rho^2 complexity terms. Lemma A.2 corrects the projection using B^{-1}, Section 5 adds a Hessian-based comparison with DoG, and Appendix D.6 explicitly restricts Q to R^d. The principal rate in Theorem 2.1 remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains parameter-free, universal dual averaging for the same six convex function classes, including simple constraints and unbounded feasible sets. The additional abstract and conclusion emphasize local-growth adaptation already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly explains how a nonzero gradient at a constrained optimum can worsen the rate, distinguishes DADA's rate adaptation from DoG's convergence guarantee, and hypothesizes that high-order smoothness explains the worst-case experiment. These refine the interpretation and applicability of largely retained results.

D1.justification: V2 documents the new sensitivity study's initialization grid and reuse of the softmax construction. Existing implementation and data-generation information is retained. The new description inconsistently calls this sensitivity to x0 while reporting variations of delta, limiting reproducibility clarity.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands related work and comparative positioning through a new subsection, Table 1.1 and Section 5. It discusses Polyak stepsizes, doubling, coin betting and bisection, adds three references, and develops the comparison with DoG. It also softens the assertion that D-Adaptation and Prodigy cannot handle constraints to saying no extension is known.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: most experiments move to Appendix E, the choice of c moves to Appendix C, and the earlier method-comparison discussion becomes an expanded Section 5 with a conclusion. Related work and explanatory passages are added. V2 also inadvertently retains two abstract blocks.

P2.justification: Most experimental figures move from the main text into Appendix E, leaving the worst-case convergence plot in Section 4. V2 adds the algorithm-property Table 1.1 and three-panel Figure E.5. The duplicated abstract also changes the first-page layout; the five original plots themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves mathematical precision through the projection and pseudocode corrections, explicit local assumptions and radius-dependent bounds. It also clarifies the comparison with DoG and adds useful initialization-sensitivity evidence. These gains outweigh the duplicated abstracts, inconsistent sensitivity-study descriptions and unsupported Prodigy wording, but those defects limit the overall improvement.
